answer:
ANSWER: None. No patient-volume group (patients_seen) shows a statistically significant (p<0.05) difference in COVID-19 severity between BCG and placebo by chi-square. Under the locked primary design — chi-square of independence on the FULL ordinal AESEV (1-4) x TRTGRP table, infected subjects only (AEPT=='COVID-19'), per-subject worst (max) AESEV, all-NaN-severity subjects excluded — the three groups give:

  group     N   BCG  Placebo   chi2    df      p        -> sig?
  1-50     106   60     46    6.974    3    0.0727      NO
  51-100    33   12     21    1.963    2    0.3748      NO
  >100       9    4      5    2.925    3    0.4033      NO

So the direct answer to 'in which patient volume group ... p<0.05' is: NONE.

The '1-50 patients seen' group is the closest and shows a consistent direction of effect (BCG had more severe cases: 9 severe(AESEV>=3) vs 2 placebo), but it is sub-threshold: p=0.0727 (ordinal) and p=0.0747 (severe>=3 vs not-severe binary sensitivity). The ordinal and binary tests AGREE (neither reaches 0.05) — no silent choice needed. The 51-100 (p~0.37) and >100 (p~0.40) groups are far from significant and underpowered.

SMALL-CELL FLAGS (expected count <5 in the ordinal table):
  1-50:    sev3 (BCG 3.96 / Plac 3.04), sev4 (BCG 2.26 / Plac 1.74)
  51-100:  sev1 BCG 4.73, sev4 BCG 0.36 / Plac 0.64  -> Fisher 2x2 (severe>=3) p=0.3636; permutation p (ordinal table) = 0.4304
  >100:    sev1, sev2, sev3, sev4 all have expected <5  -> Fisher 2x2 p=1.000; permutation p (ordinal table) = 1.000
  (Fisher's exact is well-defined only for 2x2, so for the small groups I reported it on the severe>=3 vs not-severe 2x2, plus a 50,000-perm Fisher-Freeman-Halton-style permutation p for the full ordinal table — both non-significant.)

ROBUSTNESS (conclusion unchanged across framings — no group ever reaches 0.05):
  per-AE-row ordinal: 1-50 p=0.071, 51-100 p=0.310, >100 p=0.414
  all-NaN treated as not-severe (binary): 1-50 p=0.059, 51-100 p=0.230, >100 p=1.000
  moderate-or-worse(>=2) binary: 1-50 p=0.976, 51-100 p=0.364, >100 p=1.000
  ALL 1000 subjects (no-COVID-19 as a level): 1-50 p=0.073, 51-100 p=0.334, >100 p=0.552

Bottom line: the strongest (but non-significant) signal is in the lowest-volume group (1-50 patients seen), where BCG subjects trended toward more severe COVID-19; it does not clear p<0.05 under the specified chi-square analysis or any reasonable variant.
